status: INDEX ARITHMETIC CRACKED (the last open piece). The per-depth placement-INDEX law is `placementIndex = base_constant + depth`, where `base_constant` is a COMPILE-TIME ARGUMENT pushed at each emit call site and `depth` is the build depth counter [0x5040] (0..3). Frame parity [0x521a] = (gx+gy+facing)%2 selects WHICH of a left/right base pair becomes the OR-blit's arg0c (and which the mirror arg10). This was read by HAND-DISASM of the three emit functions (wall_emit_quad 0x406c, wall_emit_corner 0x45b4, top-strips 0x4a15) where the DECOMPILER failed — capstone + manual read of the `mov ax, IMM; add ax, [bp+4]; push ax; call <orblit thunk>` idiom that repeats at every emit site. VALIDATED byte-exact against the captured liveRecords: every captured idx satisfies idx = (its family base) + depth, and the family bases match the disasm IMM constants EXACTLY (ceiling base 0x7a=122, floor base 0x96=150, top-strip bases 0x15a/0x15d/0x160/0x163/0x166/0x169 = 346/349/352/355/358/361). A reproducing function `generateSkeletonIndices(visibleDepths)` (packages/parser/src/maze/callist.ts) emits the deterministic SKELETON (ceiling 122+d / floor 150+d for the visible depths + the 6 constant top-strips) byte-exact, and exposes the full per-emit-site BASE TABLES so the side/corner/door families can be emitted once their per-depth gate state is known. Remaining gap: the per-depth GATE-SEEDING that decides which family/depth FIRES (the [0x5042]/[0x508a]/[0x5072] gate bytes the classifier sets) is medium-confidence — the index arithmetic GIVEN a fired (site,depth,parity) is HIGH confidence and byte-exact.

key_law.one_liner: placementIndex = base + depth.  arg0c (the OR/forward piece) = base_left + depth if parity==0 else base_right + depth.  arg10 (the mirror dst geom) = the opposite base + depth (0xffff if parity==0 i.e. forward OR).
key_law.depth: the build depth counter DGROUP [0x5040], 0..3 (0=party's own cell). Passed as [bp+4] to every emit fn.
key_law.parity: DGROUP [0x521a] = (gx+gy+facing)%2, computed at 0x4c45. parity==0 => the LEFT-base becomes arg0c with arg10=0xffff (a direct forward OR-blit). parity!=0 => the RIGHT-base becomes arg0c and the LEFT-base+depth becomes arg10 (a horizontal-mirror masked blit). (Per-emit some sites use a per-SPAN parity [0x521c]=(gx+gy+facing+depth)%2 instead — see emit_idioms.)
key_law.base_constants: are COMPILE-TIME IMMEDIATES pushed at each call site as a big argument block (see call_sites). They are NOT computed from geometry — they are the static placement-table SLOT IDs for each (piece-family, screen-side). The placement table (cs:[0x190], 366 records) is a fixed descriptor table; base+depth indexes the depth-banked twin within a family.
key_law.emit_thunk: every emit is `push arg10; push mode(0/1); push arg0c; call 0xfffff148` — the near-call wraps to the ega.drv FUN_0a93 OR-blit thunk. arg0c=placement idx of the source piece; arg10=0xffff (forward OR) or the mirror-dst placement idx (masked). This is exactly the (branch, arg0c, arg10) the pokeview capture records.

findings.claim: The per-depth placement INDEX = base_constant + depth, with the base a compile-time immediate argument. PROVEN by hand-disasm of wall_emit_quad (0x406c): the ceiling emit at 0x4084-0x40b2 computes arg0c = `[bp+0xe] + [bp+4]` where [bp+0xe]=0x7a=122 (the ceiling base) and [bp+4]=depth; the floor emit at 0x44ff-0x452d computes arg0c = `[bp+0x42] + [bp+4]` where [bp+0x42]=0x96=150 (the floor base). VALIDATED byte-exact vs captured liveRecords: ALL ceiling idx (122,123,124,125 at depths 0,1,2,3) satisfy idx-depth==122; ALL floor idx (150,151,152,153) satisfy idx-depth==150 — matching the disasm IMMs exactly.

findings.claim: Frame parity [0x521a]=(gx+gy+facing)%2 simultaneously (a) selects which of the LEFT/RIGHT base-pair becomes the source arg0c, and (b) selects the OR (forward, arg10=0xffff) vs masked-mirror (arg10 = the OTHER base + depth) branch. parity==0: arg10=0xffff (forward OR), arg0c=LEFT_base+depth. parity!=0: arg10=LEFT_base+depth, arg0c=RIGHT_base+depth (masked mirror). This is the EMIT-SITE manifestation of the parity OR-vs-masked branch law (maze-generation-law.json parity-selects-or-vs-masked-branch) — the WHOLE-frame branch toggle is just every emit site reading the same [0x521a]. The masked mirror geometry (dst.destX+src.destX+dst.w==40) is then a property of the placement RECORDS the two bases point at (the table stores mirror-twin geometry).

evidence.details: The idiom repeats verbatim at every emit site: `mov ax,0xffff; cmp [0x521a],0; je KEEP; mov ax,[bp+L]; add ax,[bp+4]; KEEP: push ax (arg10); mov ax,1; push ax (mode); cmp [0x521a],0; je USE_L; mov ax,[bp+R]; add ax,[bp+4]; jmp PUSH; USE_L: mov ax,[bp+L]; add ax,[bp+4]; PUSH: push ax (arg0c); call 0xfffff148`. Sites: 0x4084(ceiling), 0x44ff(floor), 0x45d0/0x4610/0x468e/0x46c2/0x4743(corner emit blocks), and the side-panel wall_emit_quad re-calls. Some sites swap [0x521a] for the per-span [0x521c]=(gx+gy+facing+depth)%2 (e.g. wall_emit_quad 0x40ca near-wall, 0x4574 trailing pair) — same idiom, alternating screen-side per depth.

findings.claim: Per build depth (loop 0x4c60), the engine calls FIVE emit fns in a fixed order, each with a big block of compile-time base IMMs (the per-family, per-screen-side placement-slot bases). The full base tables (read from the call-site disasm) are in `call_sites` below. wall_emit_quad(front, slot[0x5220]) @0x4d90 carries the CEILING (122) + near-wall (0) + FLOOR (150) bases + the front-recess bases. wall_emit_corner(corner-L, slot[0x5222]) @0x4e24 and (corner-R, slot[0x5224]) @0x4e80 carry the corner/side-wall bases (7/4/15/19/83/87/106/114/193/196/272/275/293/296 for L). wall_emit_quad(left-side, slot[0x5226]) @0x4f9b/@0x504b and (right-side, slot[0x5228]) @0x50fb/@0x51ab carry the deep side-wall family bases. The top-strips (0x4a15) carry bases 346/349/352/355/358/361 (stride 3, 6 strips), each offset by the door-phase word [0x3646] or facing — emitted ALWAYS, in every frame.

caveat_for_prior_findings: COMPLETES maze-generation-law.json's `what_is_unpinned` (the (slot-code,depth)->placement-index arithmetic). The answer: it is NOT slot-code-keyed arithmetic at all — it is `base_constant + depth` with the base a compile-time IMM argument per emit site, and slot-code only GATES whether a site fires + which shape-dispatch branch runs. The decompiler failed because the emit fns are huge flat functions with ~15 near-identical parity-branch idioms over a 30+ IMM argument block; capstone + the repeated-idiom pattern made the manual read tractable. Does NOT contradict the depth-bank structure (ceiling=122+d, floor=ceiling+28) — it EXPLAINS it: ceiling base 122, floor base 150 (=122+28), both +depth. Confirms the parity branch law at the emit-site level. Confidence HIGH for the index arithmetic; MEDIUM for the gate-seeding occlusion map (inherited).
